title.en: Volume 354 Biographies 141: Wan Chengfeng, Zhou Xiying, Qian Yue, Qin Ying, Li Zonghan, Han Dingjin, Zhu Fangzeng
title.raw: 卷354 列傳一百四十一 万承风 周系英 钱樾 秦瀛 李宗瀚 韩鼎晋 朱方增

sentences.zh: 列傳一百四十一

translations.literal: Biographies 141
translations.idiomatic: Biography 141

sentences.zh: 萬承風周系英錢樾秦瀛李宗瀚韓鼎晉朱方增

translations.literal: Wan Chengfeng, Zhou Xiying, Qian Yue, Qin Ying, Li Zonghan, Han Dingjin, and Zhu Fangzeng
translations.idiomatic: Wan Chengfeng, Zhou Xiying, Qian Yue, Qin Ying, Li Zonghan, Han Dingjin, and Zhu Fangzeng

sentences.zh: 萬承風，字和圃，江西義寧人。

translations.literal: Wan Chengfeng, style name Hepu, was a native of Yining in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Chengfeng (style Hepu) came from Yining, Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十六年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In Qianlong year 46 he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi degree in Qianlong 46, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 直上書房，侍宣宗讀。

translations.literal: He served in the Upper Study and attended the Xuanzong Emperor in his reading.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Upper Study and tutored the future Daoguang Emperor.

sentences.zh: 六十年，典試雲南。

translations.literal: In year 60 he served as chief examiner for Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year of the reign he presided over the Yunnan provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 時仁宗在潛邸，賜詩寵行。

translations.literal: At that time the Renzong Emperor was in his princely residence and bestowed a poem to honor his departure on assignment.
translations.idiomatic: The future Jiaqing Emperor, still heir in his private residence, honored him with a parting poem.

sentences.zh: 累遷翰林院侍讀。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Hanlin Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Reader in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，大考，降檢討。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing year 3, at the triennial examination, he was demoted to reviser.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaqing year 3 triennial review demoted him back to reviser.

sentences.zh: 四年，督廣東學政。

translations.literal: In year 4 he supervised as Guangdong education commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was made Guangdong education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 瓊州海寇猝發，承風以聞，命總督吉慶按治，總兵西密揚阿等以恇怯置吏議。

translations.literal: Pirates at Qionzhou suddenly erupted; Chengfeng reported it; he was ordered that Governor-General Ji Qing investigate and punish, and that Regional Commander Ximiyang'a and others be subject to official censure for cowardice.
translations.idiomatic: When pirates suddenly flared up at Qionzhou, Chengfeng memorialized the court; the throne ordered Governor-General Ji Qing to investigate and pressed disciplinary action against Regional Commander Ximiyang'a and others for cowardice.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍講學士，任滿還京，直上書房，擢詹事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Expositor of the Hanlin; when his term ended he returned to the capital, served again in the Upper Study, and was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Hanlin Expositor, he returned to Beijing at term's end, rejoined the Upper Study, and was raised to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 督山東學政，整厲士習，扶持善類。

translations.literal: As Shandong education commissioner he rectified and sharpened scholarly customs and supported men of worth.
translations.idiomatic: As Shandong education commissioner he tightened scholarly discipline and stood up for the worthy.

sentences.zh: 洊擢禮部侍郎，命還京。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and ordered to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Further promotions made him Vice Minister of Rites, then he was recalled to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 十二年，督學江蘇。

translations.literal: In year 12 he supervised studies in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he took charge of Jiangsu education.

sentences.zh: 以清江浦、荷花塘河工取勢太直，屢築屢圮，奏請復舊，詔如議行。

translations.literal: Because the Qingjiangpu and Hehuatang river works took a course too straight, repeatedly built and repeatedly collapsing, he memorialized to restore the old course; an edict approved and carried out his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The Qingjiangpu and Lotus Pond works had been routed too straight, so dikes failed again and again; he memorialized to restore the original channel, and the throne ordered it done.

sentences.zh: 調兵部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 十四年，上五旬萬壽，陳請解任還京祝嘏，詔嚴斥，左遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: In year 14, on the Emperor's fiftieth-birthday grand celebration, he petitioned to resign his post and return to the capital to offer congratulations; an edict sternly reprimanded him, and he was demoted to Grand Council academician.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14, when the court celebrated the Emperor's fiftieth birthday, he asked to leave office and return to the capital to offer congratulations; the throne rebuked him harshly and demoted him to Grand Council academician.

sentences.zh: 調安徽學政。

translations.literal: He was transferred as Anhui education commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Anhui education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 定遠士子與鳳陽胥役有隙，至試期輒修怨，當事者庇胥役，士益憤，承風疏請下巡撫嚴治胥役，置諸法。

translations.literal: Dingyuan scholars had a quarrel with Fengyang clerks and runners; when examination season came they renewed their grievances; those in charge shielded the runners, and the scholars grew more enraged; Chengfeng memorialized asking that the governor-general strictly punish the runners and place them within the law.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars in Dingyuan had fallen out with Fengyang yamen runners; each examination season revived the feud, and local officials protected the runners until the scholars' anger boiled over. Chengfeng memorialized for the governor-general to punish the runners severely and bring them to justice.

sentences.zh: 擢兵部侍郎，還京，仍直上書房，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of War, returned to the capital, again served in the Upper Study, and filled the post of lecturer at the Classics Lecture.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Vice Minister of War, he returned to Beijing, reentered the Upper Study, and served as a Classics Lecture lecturer.

sentences.zh: 十七年，引疾歸，尋卒，入祀鄉賢祠。

translations.literal: In year 17 he cited illness and retired; soon after he died and entered worship in the District Worthies Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he pleaded illness and went home; he died soon after and was enshrined in the local worthies' temple.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，追念舊學，贈禮部尚書銜，諡文恪。

translations.literal: When the Xuanzong Emperor acceded, recalling their former studies, he was posthumously granted the rank of Minister of Rites and given the posthumous title Wenké.
translations.idiomatic: When Daoguang took the throne, he remembered his old tutor and posthumously granted Chengfeng Minister of Rites rank with the posthumous name Wenké (Cultured and Reverent).

sentences.zh: 道光十二年，晉贈太傅，子方楙等加恩有差。

translations.literal: In Daoguang year 12 he was further posthumously granted Grand Tutor; his son Fangmao and others received differentiated favor.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 12 he was further ennobled as Grand Tutor, and his son Fangmao and others received graded imperial favors.

sentences.zh: 周系英，字孟才，湖南湘潭人。

translations.literal: Zhou Xiying, style name Mengcai, was a native of Xiangtan in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xiying (style Mengcai) came from Xiangtan, Hunan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十八年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，累遷侍講。

translations.literal: In Qianlong year 58 he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, was appointed compiler, and was repeatedly promoted to expositor.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Qianlong 58, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, became a compiler, and rose to expositor.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年，督四川學政。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing year 10 he supervised as Sichuan education commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 10 he was made Sichuan education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十四年，入直南書房，擢太常寺卿。

translations.literal: In year 14 he entered service in the Southern Study and was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he joined the Southern Study and was promoted Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 尋改直上書房，授三阿哥讀。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Upper Study and instructed the Third Imperial Son.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to the Upper Study to teach the third imperial son.

sentences.zh: 上諭：「不但授讀講習詩文，當教阿哥為人居心以忠厚為本。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed: "You must not only instruct in reading and lecture on poetry and prose; you should teach the prince that in one's bearing of heart, taking sincerity and generosity as the root is fundamental.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told him: "Do not only teach reading and drill him in poetry and prose—you must teach the prince that in how one carries the heart, sincerity and generosity are the foundation.

sentences.zh: 」系英請加授資治通鑑，以知古今治亂興衰之故，悉民間疾苦，上韙之。

translations.literal: " Xiying requested additionally to teach the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government, so that he might know the causes of order and disorder and rise and decline through the ages and understand the people's sufferings; the Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Xiying asked to add the Comprehensive Mirror so the prince would learn why dynasties rise and fall and know the people's hardships; the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 轉光祿寺卿，督山西學政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and supervised as Shanxi education commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He became Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Shanxi education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 任滿回京，仍直上書房。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned to the capital and again served in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: At term's end he returned to Beijing and rejoined the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 十九年，擢兵部右侍郎，母憂去，服闋，補吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In year 19 he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War; he left office on his mother's mourning; when mourning was completed he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 he was made Right Vice Minister of War, left for his mother's mourning, and after mourning filled the Vice Minister of Personnel post.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，湘潭民與江西客民閧，相殺傷，巡撫吳邦慶亦籍江西，陳奏偏袒。

translations.literal: In year 24 natives of Xiangtan and sojourning Jiangxi people clashed with mutual killing and wounding; Governor Wu Bangqing, also a Jiangxi native, memorialized with partiality.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 Xiangtan locals and Jiangxi migrants fought with casualties; Governor Wu Bangqing, himself from Jiangxi, filed a one-sided report.

sentences.zh: 系英詢齎奏人，得事始末，於召對時面陳，乃調邦慶福建，詔以獄事畀總督察治。

translations.literal: Xiying questioned the memorial bearer, learned the full account, and stated it face-to-face at imperial audience; then Bangqing was transferred to Fujian, and an edict assigned the case to the governor-general for investigation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Xiying questioned the courier, learned the whole story, and laid it out at an imperial audience; Bangqing was shifted to Fujian, and the throne handed the case to the governor-general.

sentences.zh: 系英素以樸直被眷遇，邦慶初與善，約地方事有見聞必告，至是手書言其曲直；

translations.literal: Xiying had long been favored for plainness and uprightness; Bangqing had initially been on good terms with him, agreeing that on local matters either saw something he must report; at this time he wrote by hand stating the rights and wrongs;
translations.idiomatic: Xiying had long been trusted for blunt honesty; Bangqing had once been friendly and promised to share anything he saw of local affairs—now he wrote by hand to spell out who was right and wrong;

sentences.zh: 系英子汝楨亦致書在籍給事中石承藻詢獄事：書並為邦慶得，先後以兩書上聞。

translations.literal: Xiying's son Ruzhen also wrote to the retired supervising secretary Shi Chengzao inquiring about the case; both letters were obtained by Bangqing, who successively submitted both letters to inform the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Xiying's son Ruzhen also wrote the retired censor Shi Chengzao about the case; Bangqing seized both letters and sent them up to the throne in turn.

sentences.zh: 上怒系英庇鄉人，部議革職，猶命以編修用。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry that Xiying shielded fellow-provincials; the ministry recommended dismissal from office, yet still ordered him employed as compiler.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor fumed that Xiying had favored his countrymen; the ministry recommended dismissal but still let him serve as compiler.

sentences.zh: 繼以汝楨致書事，褫職回籍。

translations.literal: Subsequently on account of Ruzhen's letter affair, he was stripped of office and returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Then, over Ruzhen's letters, he was stripped of rank and sent home.

sentences.zh: 道光初，以四品京堂召用，歷翰林院侍讀學士、內閣學士。

translations.literal: In early Daoguang he was recalled as a fourth-rank capital official and served as Hanlin Reader and Grand Council academician.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daoguang he was recalled as a fourth-rank capital official and served as Hanlin Reader and Grand Council academician.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷工部侍郎，督江西學政，尋調江蘇，許密摺言地方利病，人才臧否。

translations.literal: In year 2 he was moved to Vice Minister of Works and supervised as Jiangxi education commissioner; soon he was transferred to Jiangsu and permitted secret memorials on local benefits and harms and on talent, good and bad.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he became Vice Minister of Works and Jiangxi education commissioner, then was shifted to Jiangsu with leave to send secret memorials on local ills and on who was fit for office.

sentences.zh: 會瀕江大水，學政駐江陰，系英目擊災狀，貽書督撫，留官吏素得民者治賑務，假庫帑三萬兩購米平糶，民感之。

translations.literal: As a great flood struck along the river, the education commissioner was stationed at Jiangyin; Xiying witnessed the disaster, wrote to the governor-general and governor, retained officials who had long won the people's trust to handle relief, borrowed thirty thousand taels from the treasury to buy grain for sale at fair price, and the people were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: When floods ravaged the river counties he was stationed at Jiangyin; seeing the ruin, he wrote the governor-general and governor to keep trusted officials on relief, borrowed thirty thousand taels to buy grain and sell it fairly, and the people were grateful.

sentences.zh: 四年，調戶部左侍郎，卒於任。

translations.literal: In year 4 he was transferred to Left Vice Minister of Revenue and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was made Left Vice Minister of Revenue and died in post.

sentences.zh: 錢樾，字黼棠，浙江嘉善人。

translations.literal: Qian Yue, style name Futang, was a native of Jiashan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Yue (style Futang) came from Jiashan, Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In Qianlong year 37 he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Qianlong 37, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 典陝西鄉試，督四川學政。

translations.literal: He served as chief examiner for the Shaanxi provincial examination and supervised as Sichuan education commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Shaanxi provincial exam and served as Sichuan education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 直上書房。

translations.literal: He served in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 兩典江西鄉試，督廣西學政，累擢少詹事。

translations.literal: Twice he served as chief examiner for the Jiangxi provincial examination, supervised as Guangxi education commissioner, and was repeatedly promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He twice ran the Jiangxi provincial exam, served as Guangxi education commissioner, and rose to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，還京，仍入直。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing year 4 he returned to the capital and again entered regular service.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4 he returned to Beijing and resumed palace duty.

sentences.zh: 驟遷內閣學士、禮部侍郎，督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: He was suddenly promoted to Grand Council academician and Vice Minister of Rites and supervised as Jiangsu education commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was swiftly made Grand Council academician, Vice Minister of Rites, and Jiangsu education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時吳縣令甄輔廷治諸生糾控罪過當，學政平恕曲徇所請，斥革生員二十五人。

translations.literal: At that time the magistrate of Wu County, Zhen Futing, in trying student mutual accusations imposed penalties that were excessive; the education commissioner Pingshu bent leniently and indulged his requests, dismissing twenty-five licentiates.
translations.idiomatic: Wu County magistrate Zhen Futing had punished student accusers too harshly; Education Commissioner Pingshu, being lenient, indulged him and struck twenty-five students from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，解平恕任，以樾代，至則先复諸生名，僅坐首事者三人，士民稱慶。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of it, he removed Pingshu from his post and replaced him with Yue; on arrival Yue first restored the students' names and punished only three ringleaders; scholars and common people rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The throne heard of it, removed Pingshu, and sent Yue; Yue restored the students at once and punished only three ringleaders, to the joy of town and gown.

sentences.zh: 方其赴任，途中見行船有大書「內廷南府」者，因上疏劾姦吏詭託，上累聖明，詔飭關津禁絕，嚴罪所司。

translations.literal: As he went to his post, on the road he saw traveling boats boldly marked "Imperial Southern Bureau within the Court"; he therefore memorialized impeaching corrupt clerks for fraudulent pretense, praising the Emperor's sagacity in accumulation; an edict ordered the passes and checkpoints forbidden and closed, and sternly punished those responsible.
translations.idiomatic: On the way to his post he saw boats boldly lettered "Imperial Southern Bureau"; he memorialized against clerks trading on the name, praised the Emperor's discernment, and the court shut the passes and punished the guilty.

sentences.zh: 時南河邵壩決口，瓜、儀私梟充斥，為閭閻害，命樾密訪以聞。

translations.literal: At that time the Shao dam on the South Canal burst, and private salt smugglers filled Guazhou and Yizheng, harming the neighborhoods; he was ordered to investigate in secret and report.
translations.idiomatic: The Shao dam on the South Canal had broken, and smugglers swarmed Guazhou and Yizheng, plaguing the towns; Yue was told to investigate quietly and report.

sentences.zh: 疏陳：「黃河自豫東界至桃、宿以上，水緩沙停，致河高堤淺，所在防潰。

translations.literal: He memorialized, stating: "From the eastern border of Henan on the Yellow River up to Taoyuan and Suxian and above, the water is slow and sand settles, causing the riverbed to rise and the dikes to be shallow; everywhere guards against breach.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "From the Henan border eastward to Taoyuan and Suxian and upstream, slow water lets silt settle, raising the riverbed and shallowing the dikes—every stretch fears a breach.

sentences.zh: 請於霜降後鳩工疏正河，並增築堤防，先務所急。

translations.literal: He requested that after frost's descent labor be gathered to dredge and straighten the river and additionally heighten the dikes, first attending to what is urgent.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that after Frost's Descent crews dredge the channel and raise the dikes, tackling the worst spots first.

sentences.zh: 又以私梟為患，皆由官鹽價貴，民利食私，若稍平鹽價，則私梟自絕。

translations.literal: He also stated that private smugglers are a scourge, all because official salt is costly and the people profit by eating private salt; if the salt price were slightly leveled, then private smugglers would of themselves cease.
translations.idiomatic: On smuggling he said the root was dear government salt; ease the price and the illicit trade would die on its own.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，俱報可。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, all was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved in full.

sentences.zh: 尋調吏部，任滿回京，調戶部，兼管錢法堂事務。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel; when his term ended he returned to the capital, was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, and concurrently managed affairs of the Bureau of Currency.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to Personnel, recalled, then to Revenue, where he also ran the Bureau of Currency.

sentences.zh: 奏請申禁改漕折色，以清弊端。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting strict prohibition of altering grain tribute transport into cash commutation, to clear abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the court to forbid converting grain tribute into cash payments, to cut corruption.

sentences.zh: 復調吏部，九年，坐失察書吏舞弊，以告病治中趙曰濂虛選運同，降內閣學士，樾上疏置辯，議革職，加恩賜編修。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to the Ministry of Personnel; in year 9, on account of failure to detect clerical fraud in which the sick-leave reporting director Zhao Yuelian falsely selected a transport commissioner, he was demoted to Grand Council academician; Yue memorialized in self-defense; dismissal from office was debated, but favor granted employment as compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Personnel, in year 9 he was demoted for missing a clerk's fraud—Zhao Yuelian had rigged a transport commissioner's appointment; Yue protested in a memorial, faced dismissal, but was spared as compiler.

sentences.zh: 十年，擢鴻臚寺少卿，督山東學政。

translations.literal: In year 10 he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Banquets and supervised as Shandong education commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he became Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Banquets and Shandong education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 累遷大理寺少卿、內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and Grand Council academician.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and Grand Council academician.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，服闋，引疾不出。

translations.literal: He returned on his mother's mourning; when mourning was completed he cited illness and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: He went home for his mother's mourning; when it ended he pleaded illness and stayed out of office.

sentences.zh: 二十年，卒。

translations.literal: In year 20 he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 20.

sentences.zh: 秦瀛，字凌滄，江蘇無錫人，諭德松齡玄孫也。

translations.literal: Qin Ying, style name Lingcang, was a native of Wuxi in Jiangsu, the great-great-grandson of Tutor Songling.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Ying (style Lingcang) of Wuxi, Jiangsu, was the four-times-great-grandson of Tutor Qin Songling.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十一年，以舉人召試山東行在，授內閣中書，充軍機章京，洊遷郎中。

translations.literal: In Qianlong year 41, as a provincial graduate he was summoned to examination at the Shandong traveling palace, was appointed Grand Secretariat secretary, served as Grand Council clerk, and was repeatedly promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 41, summoned as a provincial graduate to the imperial camp in Shandong, he became a Grand Secretariat secretary, then a Grand Council clerk, and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，出為浙江溫處道，有惠政。

translations.literal: In year 58 he went out as intendant of the Wenzhou-Taichu Circuit and had benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: In year 58 he became Wenzhou-Taichu circuit intendant and governed with kindness.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，擢按察使。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing year 5 he was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 5 he was made provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 寧、紹、台三府水災，有司匿不報，瀛力言於巡撫，乃得賑。

translations.literal: The three prefectures Ningbo, Shaoxing, and Taizhou suffered flood disaster; the officials concealed and did not report; Ying spoke forcefully to the governor, and only then was relief granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningbo, Shaoxing, and Taizhou flooded, officials hid the disaster until Ying pressed the governor and relief finally came.

sentences.zh: 調湖南，衡州歲歉，有司匿不報，方議派濟陝西兵米，瀛复力言於巡撫，留米平糶。

translations.literal: Transferred to Hunan, Hengzhou had a lean year and officials concealed and did not report; just as they were discussing dispatching grain to supply Shaanxi troops, Ying again spoke forcefully to the governor and retained the grain for fair-price sale.
translations.idiomatic: In Hunan, Hengzhou's poor harvest was hushed up while grain was earmarked for Shaanxi troops; Ying again forced the governor's hand and kept the rice for fair-price sale.

sentences.zh: 七年，以病歸。

translations.literal: In year 7 he returned on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 illness sent him home.

sentences.zh: 逾兩年，起授廣東按察使，督郡縣治盜，擒著盜梁修平、吳叚喜置諸法。

translations.literal: After more than two years he was raised and appointed Guangdong surveillance commissioner, supervised the prefectures and counties in punishing bandits, and captured the notorious bandits Liang Xiuping and Wu Duanxi and placed them within the law.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was recalled as Guangdong surveillance commissioner, drove counties to hunt bandits, and executed the notorious Liang Xiuping and Wu Duanxi.

sentences.zh: 撫瓊州黎匪，嚴禁賭博白鴿票。

translations.literal: He pacified the Li bandits of Qionzhou and strictly forbade gambling and white-dove lottery tickets.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified Qionzhou's Li rebels and banned gambling and the white-dove lottery.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷浙江布政使，入覲，乞內用，授光祿寺卿，轉太常寺卿。

translations.literal: In year 10 he was transferred to Zhejiang provincial administration commissioner; on entering audience he begged for capital appointment, was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and was transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he became Zhejiang administration commissioner; at court he asked for a capital post and was made Director of Imperial Entertainments, then Director of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 疏陳廣東治盜事宜，略曰：「海盜始在高、廉，近則闌入廣州。

translations.literal: He memorialized on Guangdong measures for punishing bandits, stating in summary: "Sea bandits began in Gaozhou and Lianzhou; recently they have pushed into Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on Guangdong banditry, writing in part: "Pirates first plagued Gaozhou and Lianzhou; lately they have pushed into Guangzhou itself.

sentences.zh: 大股如鄭一、烏石二、總兵寶、朱濆等，聲勢甚張。

translations.literal: Large bands such as Zheng Yi, Wushi Er, Zongbing Bao, Zhu Fen, and others had momentum very swollen.
translations.idiomatic: Major gangs—Zheng Yi, Wushi Er, Zongbing Bao, Zhu Fen, and others—had grown terrifyingly bold.

sentences.zh: 內地順德、香山、新會三縣，連有肆劫，以馬觀、李英芳為之魁，與海盜勾結，捕急則遁入海中。

translations.literal: In the interior the three counties Shunde, Xiangshan, and Xinhui had repeated open plunder; Ma Guan and Li Yingfang were their chiefs; they colluded with sea bandits, and when pursuit was urgent they fled into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Inland, Shunde, Xiangshan, and Xinhui suffered repeated raids led by Ma Guan and Li Yingfang, who colluded with pirates and slipped to sea when pressed.

sentences.zh: 統將出海，藉詞遷延，不能盡力。

translations.literal: Commanders going to sea used pretexts to delay and could not exert full effort.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders at sea stalled on excuses and never fought at full strength.

sentences.zh: 黜提督孫全謀，而魏大斌即為之續。

translations.literal: Provincial military commander Sun Quanmou was dismissed, and Wei Dabin immediately succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Military Commander Sun Quanmou was cashiered—and Wei Dabin took his place at once.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為剿捕之法：一曰討軍實。

translations.literal: This subject's humble opinion is that methods for suppression and capture: first, investigate military realities.
translations.idiomatic: In his view, suppression required three things; first, audit the troops' real strength.

sentences.zh: 水師廢弛，則帑餉虛糜。

translations.literal: When the naval forces are lax, then treasury funds are wasted in vain.
translations.idiomatic: A slack navy only burned public money.

sentences.zh: 洋商、鹽商捐輸寬裕，經手之員尚有侵漁，遣委之將仍復驕惰，非立法痛懲，徒資耗費。

translations.literal: Foreign-trade merchants and salt merchants donate generously, yet the handling officials still embezzle; the generals dispatched remain arrogant and idle; without establishing law and stern punishment, it only supplies waste.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants gave lavishly, yet handlers skimmed and dispatched generals lounged; without stern law, donations merely fed waste.

sentences.zh: 一曰樹聲威。

translations.literal: Second, establish prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Second, build awe.

sentences.zh: 盜善偵探，非先聲讋人，盜已輕我。

translations.literal: Bandits are skilled at reconnaissance; unless first a reputation subdues men, bandits already hold us light.
translations.idiomatic: Pirates scout well; without a reputation that cowed them first, they already despised the government.

sentences.zh: 兵行之日，督撫宜舉觴歡飲；

translations.literal: On the day troops march, the governor-general and governor should raise cups and drink in celebration;
translations.idiomatic: When troops sailed, governor-general and governor should toast them off;

sentences.zh: 有功而歸，開轅行賞，不用命者，殺無赦。

translations.literal: those returning with merit should have the yamen gates opened and rewards distributed; those who do not obey orders—kill without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: victors should be welcomed at the yamen gate with rewards; disobedience meant death without mercy.

sentences.zh: 一曰戒虛飾。

translations.literal: Third, guard against empty show.
translations.idiomatic: Third, shun empty show.

sentences.zh: 擒盜豈能皆真，一念邀功，讞多失實，偶有平反，不復深咎。

translations.literal: Captured bandits cannot all be genuine; with one thought to invite merit, verdicts mostly miss truth; occasionally when cases are reversed, no further deep blame is imposed.
translations.idiomatic: Not every "bandit" caught was real; zeal for credit bred false convictions, and occasional reversals went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 嗣後總期弋獲真盜，毋縱毋枉。

translations.literal: Hereafter the overall aim should be to capture genuine bandits—neither release nor wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth he urged real captures—neither letting pirates go nor framing the innocent.

sentences.zh: 至守御之法，尤宜急講。

translations.literal: As for methods of defense, they especially should be urgently discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Defense, he said, needed equal urgency.

sentences.zh: 砲台防守口岸，口岸多而汛兵少，盜船乘間直入；

translations.literal: Gun batteries defend the river mouths, but river mouths are many and garrison troops few; bandit boats take the interval and enter straight in;
translations.idiomatic: Batteries guarded the mouths, but mouths outnumbered garrisons, so pirate craft slipped through the gaps;

sentences.zh: 巡船复少，不能禦盜，且為盜資。

translations.literal: patrol boats are also few, cannot repel bandits, and moreover supply bandits.
translations.idiomatic: patrol craft were too few to fight pirates and sometimes armed them instead.

sentences.zh: 保甲僅屬虛名，縱役訛索，反成厲政。

translations.literal: The baojia system is only an empty name; indulging runners in extortion and false demands, it instead becomes a harsh government.
translations.idiomatic: Baojia existed in name only; yamen runners extorted under its cover until it became a scourge.

sentences.zh: 欲行保甲團練，先須百姓服從。

translations.literal: To implement baojia and militia training, first the common people must be made to obey.
translations.idiomatic: To make baojia and militia work, the people had to trust the government first.

sentences.zh: 臣以為嚴防守必先澄清吏治，澄吏治必先固民心。

translations.literal: This subject considers that strict defense must first clarify official administration, and clarifying official administration must first solidify popular hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Strict defense, he argued, required clean government; clean government required winning the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 一曰清獄訟。

translations.literal: First, clear lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: First, clear the courts.

sentences.zh: 粵民好訟，大小案件，諭旨嚴飭，尚多沉擱。

translations.literal: Guangdong people are fond of litigation; large and small cases, though edicts sternly admonish, still many lie submerged and shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong folk loved lawsuits; despite stern edicts, cases large and small still piled up untouched.

sentences.zh: 殆由案之初起，遲延不辦，土棍訟師，從而把持，遂至供情屢易，莫可窮究。

translations.literal: Probably because when a case first arises, delay in handling it lets local bullies and litigation masters take hold in succession, until testimony repeatedly changes and nothing can be thoroughly investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Likely because slow handling at the start let thugs and pettifoggers seize each file, testimony shifted again and again, and truth became impossible to find.

sentences.zh: 惟有督飭州縣，有一案即清一案，務洗慵惰偏私之習。

translations.literal: Only by supervising and urging the prefectures and counties—clearing each case as soon as there is a case—can one strive to wash away habits of laziness and partiality for private interest.
translations.idiomatic: Only by pressing prefectures and counties to clear every case as it arose could the habits of sloth and private favor be scrubbed away.

sentences.zh: 一曰抑冗濫。

translations.literal: One says: restrain redundancy and excess.
translations.idiomatic: Second, curb bloated staffs and pointless posts.

sentences.zh: 六計尚廉，近海州縣有緝捕解犯之責，尤宜撙節，庶不虧倉庫而累閭閻。

translations.literal: The six evaluations esteem integrity; coastal prefectures and counties bear duties of pursuit, capture, and escorting prisoners, and should especially practice thrift, so that the granaries are not depleted and the neighborhoods not burdened.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Evaluations prize integrity; seaboard counties that must chase fugitives and escort prisoners above all needed thrift, lest granaries run dry and villages bear the cost.

sentences.zh: 一令到任，幕友長隨，多人坐食，勢不能復為廉吏。

translations.literal: When one magistrate arrives to take office, staff counselors and long-attendant followers—many sit and eat salary—and the trend makes it impossible again to be an upright official.
translations.idiomatic: Once a magistrate took his post, a swarm of secretaries and hangers-on lived off his table; under that weight no man could stay honest.

sentences.zh: 雜職武弁，惟利是圖，稍授以權，即挾製文吏。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous-rank military officers seek only profit; given a little authority, they immediately coerce and control civil officials.
translations.idiomatic: Petty military officers chased profit alone; grant them the slightest power and they bent civil officials to their will.

sentences.zh: 雜職差委過多，亦滋擾累。

translations.literal: Too many miscellaneous appointments for duties also breed harassment and burdens.
translations.idiomatic: Too many petty commissions only bred fresh harassment.

sentences.zh: 一日懲蠹役。

translations.literal: Third: punish corrupt runners.
translations.idiomatic: Third, punish corrupt yamen runners.

sentences.zh: 胥役熟習地方情形，串同官親家屬，肆為民害。

translations.literal: Runners are well versed in local conditions; in collusion with officials' kin and household members, they wantonly harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: Runners knew every local angle; with magistrates' kin they colluded and preyed on the people.

sentences.zh: 廣東胥役，每有暗通盜匪，收受陋規，此尤不可不嚴行懲創也。

translations.literal: Guangdong runners often secretly communicate with bandits and robbers and receive crude customary fees—this especially must not escape stern punishment and correction.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangdong, runners often tipped off pirates and took illicit fees—there, he urged, punishment had to be merciless.

sentences.zh: 三者既舉而吏治澄，吏治澄而民心固，於以舉行保甲團練，無不可使之民，即無不可行之法矣。

translations.literal: Once these three are undertaken, official administration clears; when official administration clears, popular hearts are firm—with that, implementing baojia and militia training, there are no people who cannot be made to obey, and no laws that cannot be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Carry out all three, he argued, and government would clear; clear government would steady the people; then baojia and militia could bind any community and enforce any rule.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，詔下疆吏採行。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted; an edict sent it down to frontier officials for adoption and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial went up; the throne ordered frontier officials to put it into practice.

sentences.zh: 遷順天府尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In year 12 he was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he was promoted Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 以宗室敏學獄會擬輕縱，議褫職，詔原之，左遷光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: Because in the imperial clansman Minxue case the joint deliberation was deemed unduly lenient, dismissal from office was debated; an edict pardoned him, and he was demoted laterally to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: When a joint verdict in the clansman Minxue case was judged too lenient, the court debated stripping his post; the emperor spared him but demoted him to Director of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 歷左副都御史、倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: He served as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grain Depot Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grain Depot Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 詔整頓倉場，慮瀛齒衰，以二品頂戴調左副都御史。

translations.literal: Ordered to rectify the grain depots, fearing Ying's age was declining, he was transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief with second-rank hat finial.
translations.idiomatic: Tasked with reforming the grain depots, the court feared Ying's years and moved him to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief with a second-rank finial.

sentences.zh: 尋授兵部侍郎，復調刑部。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Minister of War, then transferred back to Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Vice Minister of War, then returned to Justice.

sentences.zh: 瀛治獄平慎，在浙辨定海難民十二人非盜。

translations.literal: Ying judged cases with equanimity and caution; in Zhejiang he distinguished twelve Dinghai refugees as not bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Ying tried cases with calm care; in Zhejiang he proved twelve Dinghai refugees were no pirates.

sentences.zh: 及海盜誣攀族人，已入告，卒更正省釋。

translations.literal: When sea bandits falsely implicated his clansmen and a charge had already been entered, he finally corrected it and secured release.
translations.idiomatic: When pirates framed his kinsmen and indictments were already filed, he overturned the case and won their release.

sentences.zh: 在部治運丁盜米，訐者謂以藥置米中立溢，試之不驗，仁宗親試明其枉，尤為時稱。

translations.literal: At the ministry he tried grain-transport laborers for stealing rice; accusers said medicine placed in the rice caused it to swell upright; tested, it did not verify; Emperor Renzong personally tested and clarified the injustice—especially praised in the age.
translations.idiomatic: At the ministry he tried transport coolies for stealing rice; accusers claimed drugs swelled the grain in the sack—tests failed, and Emperor Renzong's own trial exposed the frame-up, winning wide praise.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以病解任。

translations.literal: In year 15 he resigned on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 illness ended his tenure.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，卒。

translations.literal: In Daoguang year 1 he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Daoguang 1.

sentences.zh: 瀛工文章，與姚鼐相推重，體亦相近雲。

translations.literal: Ying was skilled in literary composition and mutually esteemed with Yao Nai; their styles were also said to be similar.
translations.idiomatic: Ying wrote well and held Yao Nai in mutual esteem; their prose was said to be much alike.

sentences.zh: 李宗瀚，字春湖，江西臨川人。

translations.literal: Li Zonghan, style name Chunhu, was a native of Linchuan in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zonghan (style Chunhu) came from Linchuan, Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十八年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In Qianlong year 58 he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Qianlong 58, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，大考二等，擢左贊善。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing year 3, in the great examination he placed second class and was promoted to Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 3 he ranked second class in the palace examination and was made Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍講學士，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Erudite Lecturer, and served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder of the Emperor's Movements.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Erudite Lecturer and served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder of the Emperor's Movements.

sentences.zh: 五年，典福建鄉試，母憂歸，服闋，補原官，轉侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In year 5 he served as chief examiner for the Fujian provincial examination; on his mother's mourning he returned home; when mourning was completed he resumed his former post and was transferred to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he ran the Fujian provincial exam; his mother's death sent him home, and after mourning he resumed office as Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 九年，督湖南學政，歷太僕寺卿、宗人府丞、左副都御史。

translations.literal: In year 9 he supervised as Hunan education commissioner, and served as Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, Deputy Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he became Hunan education commissioner, then Director of the Imperial Stud, Deputy Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 二十年，丁本生母憂，服闋，在籍奏請終生祖母養，允之。

translations.literal: In year 20 he observed mourning for his biological mother; when mourning was completed, while at home he memorialized requesting to spend his life caring for his biological paternal grandmother, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he mourned his birth mother; when mourning ended he asked from home to spend his life nursing his birth father's grandmother, and the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 道光三年，遭祖母喪。

translations.literal: In Daoguang year 3 he suffered his grandmother's death.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 3 his grandmother died.

sentences.zh: 先是禮臣建議，為父後者為生祖母終三年喪，宗瀚幸奉功令，既而部議仍改期服，宗瀚本生父秉禮已老，而有子四人，以出繼不得終養。

translations.literal: Earlier the Ministry of Rites had proposed that one who has become heir after the father should observe three-year mourning for the biological paternal grandmother; Zonghan was fortunate to follow that merit decree, but thereafter the ministry deliberation still changed it to one-year mourning; Zonghan's biological father Bingli was already old, yet had four sons—because he had been given out in adoption, he could not complete the life-long care.
translations.idiomatic: Rites officials had ruled that an heir in his father's line should mourn a birth grandmother three years; Zonghan briefly rejoiced at the decree, but the ministry soon reverted to one-year mourning. His birth father Bingli was aged, with four sons, yet Zonghan—given in adoption—could no longer keep the lifelong care he had promised.

sentences.zh: 五年，入都，召見，詢家世官資甚悉。

translations.literal: In year 5 he entered the capital; summoned to audience, he was questioned in great detail on family background and official credentials.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he came to the capital; the emperor received him and questioned his family and career in minute detail.

sentences.zh: 宗瀚具陳終養始末，宣宗為之嗟嘆，遂補原官。

translations.literal: Zonghan fully stated the beginning and end of his life-long care; the Xuanzong Emperor sighed over it for him and then restored his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan told the whole story of his years at his grandmother's side; the Xuanzong Emperor sighed in sympathy and restored his former post.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢工部侍郎，典浙江鄉試，留學政。

translations.literal: In year 8 he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works, served as chief examiner for the Zhejiang provincial examination, and remained as education commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he became Vice Minister of Works, ran the Zhejiang provincial exam, and stayed on as education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一年，丁本生父憂，哀毀，扶病奔喪，卒於衢州，以衰服殮，年六十三。

translations.literal: In year 11 he observed mourning for his biological father; in grief he ruined his health, and supporting illness he rushed to the funeral—he died at Quzhou and was encoffined in mourning garments, age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 his birth father died; grief shattered him, and he dragged himself to the funeral only to die at Quzhou, where he was buried in full mourning dress at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 宗瀚孝謹恬退，中歲以養親居林下十年，書法尤為世重。

translations.literal: Zonghan was filial, cautious, and retiring in spirit; in mid-life he dwelt ten years in the woods to care for kin, and his calligraphy was especially prized by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Filial, careful, and self-effacing, he spent a decade in retirement mid-career to nurse his elders; his calligraphy the age prized above all.

sentences.zh: 韓鼎晉，字樹屏，四川長壽人。

translations.literal: Han Dingjin, style name Shuping, was a native of Changshou in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Dingjin (style Shuping) came from Changshou, Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆六十年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In Qianlong year 60 he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Qianlong 60, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶九年，改御史。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing year 9 he was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 9 he became a censor.

sentences.zh: 疏言天主教流傳之害，請申禁以絕根株，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized on the harm of Catholicism's spread and requested strict prohibition to cut off the roots; the request was followed.
translations.idiomatic: He warned of Catholicism's spread and asked a strict ban to uproot it; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 以母老請終養，十六年，服闋，補原官。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he requested life-long care at home; in year 16, when mourning was completed, he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: His mother aged, he asked to care for her at home; in year 16, mourning done, he took up his old post.

sentences.zh: 疏陳四川積弊六事，曰：禁科派以安閭閻，除啯匪以防積漸，查卡房以全民命，禁拐騙以警貪頑，嚴攤捐以養廉潔，覈戎政以歸實效。

translations.literal: He memorialized on six long-standing abuses of Sichuan, saying: forbid irregular levies to settle the neighborhoods; eliminate gufei bandits to guard against gradual spread; investigate checkpoint houses to preserve people's lives; forbid kidnapping swindles to warn the greedy and stubborn; strictly regulate stall levies to nurture integrity; audit military administration to return to real results.
translations.idiomatic: He listed six Sichuan abuses: end illegal levies to ease villages; crush gufei gangs before they spread; shut abusive checkpoints; stop kidnapping rackets to warn the greedy; tighten stall taxes to keep officials honest; and audit military affairs for real effect.

sentences.zh: 又言京師賭風大熾，多屬王公大臣輿夫設局，倚勢骫法，帝命指實，下詔嚴治。

translations.literal: He also said that gambling in the capital blazed fiercely, mostly set up by princes, grandees, and chair-bearers of great ministers, who leaned on power and bent the law; the emperor ordered concrete identification, and an edict sternly punished it.
translations.idiomatic: He also charged that Beijing gambling ran wild, often run by princes, ministers, and their sedan-chair bearers, who bent the law by rank; the emperor demanded names and issued a stern purge.

sentences.zh: 逾日，獲賭案三，大學士、步軍統領祿康輿夫為之魁。

translations.literal: The next day three gambling cases were seized; Grand Secretary and Steppe Brigade Commander Lu Kang's chair-bearers were their ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: Next day three gambling rings fell; the ringleaders were chair-bearers of Grand Secretary Lu Kang, who also commanded the Steppe Brigade.

sentences.zh: 親貴近臣，莫不悚息​​。

translations.literal: Kin of the imperial house and close ministers—none did not tremble in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kin and court favorites alike trembled.

sentences.zh: 巡視山東漕務，轉工科給事中、光祿寺少卿，督陝甘學政。

translations.literal: He inspected Shandong grain-transport affairs, was transferred to Supervising Secretary of the Ministry of Works, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and supervised as Shaanxi-Gansu education commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected Shandong grain transport, became a Works supervising secretary and Vice Director of Imperial Entertainments, then Shaanxi-Gansu education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「榆、綏諸州縣倉貯空虛，宜設法籌補，其地資蒙古糧食接濟。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The prefectures and counties of Yulin and Suide and others have empty granary stores; methods should be devised to make up the shortfall; those regions rely on Mongol grain for relief.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Yulin, Suide, and neighboring counties have empty granaries and need replenishment; the region depends on Mongol grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 今腹裡邊外俱荒，當分別安置撫卹。

translations.literal: Now both the interior heartland and the outer borderlands are stricken; they should be separately settled and comforted with relief."
translations.idiomatic: Famine now grips both interior and frontier alike; each district needs its own relief and resettlement."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「南山善後事宜，宜行堅壁清野之法。

translations.literal: " He also said: "For postwar matters in the Southern Mountains, the method of fortifying villages and clearing the countryside should be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged for the Southern Mountains after the rebellion: "Fortify villages and clear the countryside.

sentences.zh: 山內流民雜處，最為奸藪，當嚴行保甲，使姦宄無所匿。

translations.literal: Within the mountains displaced persons mix together—it is most a nest of villains; baojia should be strictly enforced so that villains have nowhere to hide.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees crowd the hills—the worst nest of rogues; enforce baojia strictly so criminals have nowhere to hide.

sentences.zh: 軍中擄脅難民子女，請嚴禁。

translations.literal: In the army, seizing and coercing refugee men and women and children—he requested strict prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: He asked a strict ban on troops seizing refugee women and children.

sentences.zh: 南山附近及豫東並經兵燹，宜慎選牧令，以蘇民氣。

translations.literal: The Southern Mountains vicinity and eastern Henan alike have passed through warfare and fire; magistrates should be carefully chosen to revive popular morale.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Mountains and eastern Henan, scarred by war, need magistrates chosen with care to revive the people's spirit.

sentences.zh: 川北荒歉，與陝、甘毗連，鹽梟啯匪多出其中，請先事豫防。

translations.literal: Northern Sichuan is stricken with famine and borders Shaanxi and Gansu; salt smugglers and gufei bandits mostly emerge from among them—he requested prior preventive measures.
translations.idiomatic: Famine in northern Sichuan, adjoining Shaanxi and Gansu, breeds salt smugglers and gufei gangs—he asked preventive action before they spread.

sentences.zh: 」並下疆吏如所請行。

translations.literal: " All were sent down to frontier officials to act as requested.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne sent all of it to frontier officials to execute.

sentences.zh: 歷鴻臚寺卿、通政司副使、太常寺卿、左副都御史。

translations.literal: He served as Director of the Court of Imperial Banquets, Vice Director of the Office of Transmission, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director of Imperial Banquets, Vice Director of Transmission, Director of Imperial Sacrifices, and Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，命察視近畿水災，督黃村賑務。

translations.literal: In year 24 he was ordered to inspect flood disaster in the near capital region and to supervise relief at Huangcun.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 he was sent to survey floods near the capital and oversee relief at Huangcun.

sentences.zh: 督福建學政，疏言：「閩中吏治久窳，請不限資格，用廉幹吏補汀、漳、泉三郡望緊要缺，久其任以專責成。

translations.literal: As Fujian education commissioner he memorialized: "Official administration in Fujian has long been corrupt; I request that qualifications not be limited, and that upright, capable officials be used to fill the high-demand urgent posts of the three prefectures Tingzhou, Zhangzhou, and Quanzhou, extending their tenure to concentrate responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: As Fujian education commissioner he wrote: "Fujian government has rotted for years; waive seniority and send able, honest men to the urgent posts in Tingzhou, Zhangzhou, and Quanzhou, and keep them long enough to answer for results.

sentences.zh: 漳、泉營伍通盜，請責提鎮立予重典，勿稍袒庇。

translations.literal: The garrisons of Zhangzhou and Quanzhou collude with bandits; I request that the provincial commander and regional commander be charged to impose heavy punishment at once, without the slightest sheltering.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzhou and Quanzhou troops trade with pirates; hold the provincial and regional commanders to swift, heavy punishment—no favoritism."

sentences.zh: 」道光六年，遷倉場侍郎，以病罷。

translations.literal: " In Daoguang year 6 he was transferred to Grain Depot Vice Minister and resigned on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 6 he became Grain Depot Vice Minister, then quit for illness.

sentences.zh: 起補工部侍郎，京察，原品休致。

translations.literal: He was raised and appointed Vice Minister of Works; in the capital evaluation, he retired at his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Vice Minister of Works, he passed the capital evaluation and retired at full rank.

sentences.zh: 卒於家，祀鄉賢祠。

translations.literal: He died at home and was enshrined in the Local Worthies Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home and entered the Local Worthies Temple.

sentences.zh: 朱方增，字虹舫，浙江海鹽人。

translations.literal: Zhu Fangzeng, style name Hongfang, was a native of Haiyan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fangzeng (style Hongfang) came from Haiyan, Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing year 6 he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Jiaqing 6, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 典雲南鄉試，遷國子監司業。

translations.literal: He served as chief examiner for the Yunnan provincial examination and was transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He ran the Yunnan provincial exam and became Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 十八年，教匪之變，方增劾直隸總督溫承惠貽誤地方，黜之。

translations.literal: In year 18, at the outbreak of the Teaching Bandit rebellion, Fangzeng impeached Zhili Governor-General Wen Chenghui for misleading and harming the region, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18, when the Teaching Bandit rising broke out, Fangzeng impeached Zhili Governor-General Wen Chenghui for bungling the province and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 應詔陳言，論用人理財，略曰：「近今大臣中，罕有以進賢為務者。

translations.literal: In response to an edict he stated his views, discussing employment of men and management of finances, stating in summary: "Among great ministers in recent times, few make advancing the worthy their task.
translations.idiomatic: Answering an imperial call for views on appointments and finance, he wrote in part: "Few ministers lately make promoting talent their business.

sentences.zh: 蓋薦舉之事，易於徇私，黨援交結，不得不防，而大臣亦遂引嫌自避。

translations.literal: For recommendation and selection easily lend themselves to private favor; factional support and mutual entanglement cannot but be guarded against—yet great ministers also then cite scruple and avoid on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Recommendations invite favoritism and clique ties, so ministers must guard against them—yet many now dodge the duty altogether out of scruple.

sentences.zh: 夫大臣避徇私之名，而忘以人事君之責，所謂因噎廢食，非公忠體國者所宜有也。

translations.literal: Great ministers who avoid the name of private favor yet forget the duty of serving the ruler through men—this is what is called stopping eating for fear of choking; it is not what those of public loyalty who embody the state should have.
translations.idiomatic: To shun the charge of cronyism while neglecting the duty to put the right men before the throne is to choke on fear of choking—no true servant of the realm should do it.

sentences.zh: 至於任用之方，則無過於考言詢事。

translations.literal: As for the method of employment, nothing surpasses examining words and inquiring into affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For appointments, nothing beats testing words against deeds.

sentences.zh: 皇上博訪週諮，徐為印證。

translations.literal: Your Majesty broadly inquires and consults everywhere, and slowly verifies.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty already asks widely and listens everywhere; verify slowly.

sentences.zh: 於召對時，各就所長，諭使面陳，果能洞悉原委，又當試之以事，以觀其能踐與否。

translations.literal: At audiences summoned to court, each according to his strength should be instructed to state face to face; if he can truly penetrate origin and detail, then he should also be tried with affairs, to observe whether he can carry them out or not.
translations.idiomatic: At audience, let each man speak to his strength; if he truly grasps a matter's roots, set him a task and see whether he delivers.

sentences.zh: 如或敷奏並無條理，則其人固不足用，而大臣之識見優絀，心地公私，亦可見矣。

translations.literal: If in presentation there is altogether no order, then that person is inherently not fit for use—and the great minister's discernment superior or inferior, and the public or private cast of his heart, can also be seen.
translations.idiomatic: If his answers lack all order, the man is useless—and the recommending minister's judgment and private motives stand revealed.

sentences.zh: 抑臣思臣工居職，苟非闒茸齷齪者流，孰不思自效？

translations.literal: Yet this subject considers that officials in office, if they are not the sort who are incompetent and filthy, who does not think to offer his effort?
translations.idiomatic: Yet which official, unless incompetent or corrupt, does not wish to serve?

sentences.zh: 況蒙皇上訓飭至再至三，而猶故習相仍，驟難振拔者，良有數端：條例過繁，文案蒨屑，雖有強敏之吏，而精神疲於具文，其實關於政治民生，轉致不能詳覈。

translations.literal: Moreover, having received Your Majesty's admonitions again and again, yet old habits continue in succession and are suddenly hard to pull up—there are truly several causes: regulations too numerous, documents minute and trivial; though there are forceful and keen officials, their spirit is exhausted on paperwork, while what truly concerns government and people's livelihoods in turn cannot be thoroughly audited.
translations.idiomatic: And though Your Majesty has warned them again and again, old habits linger and reform comes hard—for several reasons: rules multiply and paperwork swallows clerks, so even sharp men exhaust themselves on forms while matters that touch people's lives go unchecked.

sentences.zh: 一也。

translations.literal: That is the first.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first.

sentences.zh: 差務絡繹，公私賠累，身家之卹不遑，民物之懷漸恝。

translations.literal: Commissioned duties come in continuous streams; public and private losses pile up; care for one's household has no leisure, and concern for the people's welfare gradually grows indifferent.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioned errands never cease; public duty and private purse both bleed; officials cannot shelter their families, and care for the people fades.

sentences.zh: 二也。

translations.literal: That is the second.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second.

sentences.zh: 訐告之風，至今益甚。

translations.literal: The wind of accusation and denunciation, to this day, grows ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: The plague of informers grows worse by the year.

sentences.zh: 嘗有以田土、鬥毆細故而叩閽京控者，有司畏其挾制，不得不姑息委蛇。

translations.literal: There have been those who, over trifles of fields or brawls, beat the palace gates and appeal to Beijing for control; the officials fear their leverage and cannot but indulge and temporize.
translations.idiomatic: Men sue over field spats and fistfights by rushing to Beijing; magistrates fear their leverage and temporize.

sentences.zh: 雖有急公自好者，其尋常蒨屑之事，豈皆一一可達聖聰？

translations.literal: Though there are those eager for the public good and self-respecting, can their ordinary minute and trivial affairs all one by one reach the sage's ear?
translations.idiomatic: Even earnest officials cannot bring every petty quarrel before the throne.

sentences.zh: 甚至匿名揭帖，無主名之可指。

translations.literal: Some go so far as anonymous placards with no master name that can be pointed to.
translations.idiomatic: Anonymous placards appear with no accuser to name.

sentences.zh: 蠹吏猾胥，奸民惡僕，求謀不遂，懲治過嚴，皆可造作飛語，訐及陰私。

translations.literal: Corrupt clerks, cunning runners, wicked commoners, and vicious servants—when schemes fail, or punishment is too stern—all can fabricate flying rumors and accuse private matters.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt clerks, sly runners, rogues, and vicious servants—foiled in a scheme or punished too hard—invent slander and denounce private lives.

sentences.zh: 足使任事之心，不寒而栗，委曲隱忍。

translations.literal: Enough to make the heart of one who undertakes affairs shiver without cold and bend in concealment and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Enough to make any man who takes responsibility shiver and yield in silence.

sentences.zh: 姦宄橫行，大都由此。

translations.literal: Villains running rampant—mostly proceed from this.
translations.idiomatic: Most villainy abroad springs from this.

sentences.zh: 三也。

translations.literal: That is the third.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third.

sentences.zh: 今皇上欲整飭因循積習，臣愚以為必先除此三者之弊，庶廓然無所疑畏，而得專精實政矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty wishes to rectify lingering habits of routine and long accumulation; this subject's humble opinion is that one must first remove the abuses of these three, so that broadly there is nothing to doubt or fear, and one can obtain concentrated effort on real administration.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty means to break entrenched habit, I believe these three abuses must go first; then officials will act without fear and give their full strength to real government.

sentences.zh: 經國之方，理財尤要。

translations.literal: The method of ordering the state—managing finances is especially important.
translations.idiomatic: To govern a realm, sound finance matters most.

sentences.zh: 古者以三十年之通制國用，斟酌盈虛，量入為出，用能經常不匱。

translations.literal: Antiquity used thirty years' overall reckoning to regulate state expenditure, weighing surplus and deficit, measuring income to set outgo, and thereby could make regular supply never exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity planned the treasury on thirty years' totals, balancing surplus and deficit and matching outlay to income, so the state never ran dry.

sentences.zh: 今戶部歲入歲出，年一匯奏。

translations.literal: Today the Ministry of Revenue's yearly income and yearly outgo are reported once a year in summary memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Ministry of Revenue reports income and outlay once a year.

sentences.zh: 惟中外未合為一，條緒繁賾，極難釐剔。

translations.literal: Only capital and provinces are not united as one; threads of categories are numerous and tangled, extremely hard to sort and pick clear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet capital accounts and provinces are never unified; the lines of revenue are hopelessly tangled.

sentences.zh: 且凡撥解即謂之出，並未實計所用。

translations.literal: Moreover, whenever funds are allocated and forwarded, that is called outgo, yet the actual amount used is not reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: Any transfer counts as spent before anyone tracks what was actually used.

sentences.zh: 新舊牽溷，凌雜益甚，而出納諸款，又因有無定之款，盈朒參差。

translations.literal: Old and new are dragged together in confusion, disorder piles ever higher, and among receipts and disbursements the various items again suffer from items of uncertain existence, surplus and deficit uneven.
translations.idiomatic: Old and new entries blur together; receipts and payments mix fixed and uncertain items until surplus and deficit cannot be told apart.

sentences.zh: 以故一歲之中，所出幾何，覈之所入，贏餘若干，不能得其實數。

translations.literal: For this reason, within one year, how much went out, audited against what came in, how much surplus—one cannot obtain the real numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Thus within a single year no one can state true outlays, true income, or true surplus.

sentences.zh: 請旨敕下戶部，歲入歲出，宜合中外為一。

translations.literal: I request an imperial command sent down to the Ministry of Revenue: yearly income and yearly outgo should unite capital and provinces as one.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to order the Ministry of Revenue to merge capital and provincial accounts into one ledger.

sentences.zh: 核計贏餘總數，仍取前一二歲所贏餘，確實比較，然後審其輕重緩急，舉一切例內例外諸用款，有可裁省停緩者，酌加撙節。

translations.literal: Calculate the total surplus, still taking the surpluses of the previous one or two years for solid comparison, and then examine what is light or heavy, urgent or slow, setting forth all items of expenditure within and outside precedent that can be cut, suspended, or slowed, and add thrift as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Total the surplus, compare it honestly with the prior year or two, weigh each expense by urgency, and cut, defer, or trim every routine and exceptional charge that allows.

sentences.zh: 庶合於古人通年制用之法，而度支充裕矣。

translations.literal: Then it may accord with the ancients' method of regulating expenditure by overall years, and the fiscal accounts will be ample.
translations.idiomatic: Then spending would match the ancients' multi-year planning, and the treasury would stand secure.

sentences.zh: 二十年，入直懋勤殿，編纂石渠寶笈、秘殿珠林。

translations.literal: In year 20 he entered regular service in the Hall of Imperial Quickening and compiled the Stone Canal Precious Collection and the Secret Hall Pearl Forest.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he joined duty in the Hall of Imperial Quickening to compile the Stone Canal Precious Collection and the Secret Hall Pearl Forest.

sentences.zh: 尋督廣西學政，累遷翰林院侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Soon he supervised as Guangxi education commissioner and was repeatedly promoted to Hanlin Academy Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Guangxi education commissioner and rose to Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 道光四年，大考第一，擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: In Daoguang year 4, in the great examination he placed first and was promoted to Grand Council academician.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 4 he topped the palace examination and was made Grand Council academician.

sentences.zh: 典山東鄉試。

translations.literal: He served as chief examiner for the Shandong provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Shandong provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 七年，督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: In year 7 he supervised as Jiangsu education commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he became Jiangsu education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒。

translations.literal: In year 10 he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 10.

sentences.zh: 方增熟諳朝章典故，輯國史名臣事蹟，為從政觀法錄，行於世。

translations.literal: Fangzeng was well versed in court regulations and precedents; he compiled the deeds of famous ministers in the national histories into Records for Observing Models in Governing, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Fangzeng knew court ritual and precedent inside out; he compiled notable ministers' careers from the dynastic histories into Records for Observing Models in Governing, a book that circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 論曰：萬承風、周系英、錢樾以侍從之臣，軺車所至，建白卓然。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Wan Chengfeng, Zhou Xiying, and Qian Yue, as attendant ministers—wherever their light carriages reached, their proposals and reports stood out prominently.
translations.idiomatic: The historian concludes: as palace tutors, Wan Chengfeng, Zhou Xiying, and Qian Yue left a striking record of memorials wherever their tours took them.

sentences.zh: 秦瀛之治績，李宗瀚之孝行，非僅以文藻稱。

translations.literal: Qin Ying's achievements in governing, Li Zonghan's conduct of filial piety—they are not praised only for literary ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Ying's administrative record and Li Zonghan's filial devotion were admired for more than fine prose.

sentences.zh: 韓鼎晉、朱方增侃侃獻納，言有體要，皆風采著於朝列矣。

translations.literal: Han Dingjin and Zhu Fangzeng offered their views with ease and confidence; their words had substance and key points—all had their presence and distinction shown in the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Han Dingjin and Zhu Fangzeng spoke up forthrightly with weight and point; each cut a memorable figure in the halls of court.
